core_principles.text: Maintain the anatomical curves of the spine and a straight body alignment from the shoulder joint to the knees or ankles throughout the movement.
Place the hands straight under the shoulders so the shoulder joint is directly over the wrist joint with the middle finger under the acromioclavicular joint.
Lower the body toward the floor until achieving 90 degrees of elbow flexion, bringing the chest as close to the ground as possible before pushing up.

common_mistakes.text: Allowing incorrect and damaging inclinations of the torso during the push-up.

specific_findings.text: Elevating the hands above the feet displays the lowest mean value of vertical force and a low rate of force development (RFD).
The standard push-up position displays the highest rate of force development (RFD) and the highest activation of the triceps brachii muscle.

consequences.text: Failing to maintain a correct upright posture during push-ups creates damaging inclinations of the torso, placing stress on the spine.

core_principles.text: Performing push-ups from the knees instead of the toes reduces stress on the glenohumeral joint while maintaining similar muscle activation levels.
Placing an unstable surface under the upper extremities is required to effectively increase muscle activation during push-up variations.

common_mistakes.text: Allowing the serratus anterior to fatigue or weaken during push-ups alters normal scapular motion.

specific_findings.text: Knee push-ups produce almost the same electromyographic activity in most muscle groups as standard push-ups on toes.
The push-up plus caused an average anterior deltoid activation of 103% MVC and a peak activation of 185% MVC during maximum force application.
Isometric plank support on the elbows and soles with the body parallel to the ground resulted in a 54% activation increase in the quadratus lumborum muscle.
Pectoralis major activation remains unaffected by support surface stability during push-ups.

consequences.text: Weakness or fatigue in the serratus anterior decreases upward scapular rotation, causing the peak of the scapula to shift forward and upward, which increases shoulder injury risk.

core_principles.text: Place the hands directly under the glenohumeral joint with the palms parallel when setting up a standard push-up.
Maintain straight alignment between the shoulder, ischium, and lateral malleolus throughout the push-up.
Lower the body during the push-up until the elbows reach an inclination of 90 degrees.

specific_findings.text: The study evaluated 11 healthy participants with an average age of 22.5 ± 2.4 years, height of 177.7 ± 5.2 cm, weight of 75.9 ± 6.1 kg, and BMI under 25.

core_principles.text: Maintain full body alignment throughout the push-up movement.
Lower the pelvis and torso simultaneously when performing a knee push-up.

specific_findings.text: Elevating the hands 30 cm above the feet significantly reduces vertical force on both upper extremities compared to standard, wide, diamond, knee, and feet-elevated push-up positions (p<0.05).

Placing the hands in a close diamond position results in lower vertical force on the left upper extremity compared to standard and wide positions, but higher vertical force than elevating the hands (p<0.05).
Rate of Force Development (RFD) in the left upper extremity is significantly higher during standard push-ups compared to close-hand diamond push-ups (p<0.05).
Rate of Force Development (RFD) in the right upper extremity is significantly lower in the hands-elevated push-up position compared to the feet-elevated push-up position (p<0.05).

core_principles.text: Push-up position variations that maximize triceps brachii activation can be utilized specifically to target and strengthen the triceps brachii muscle.
Push-up variations that produce a lower rate of force development and slower muscle activation are not recommended when the primary goal is improving rapid dynamic strength.

specific_findings.text: Right-handed participants applied a higher percentage of average relative force on the left upper extremity across all tested push-up positions.
Maximum activation of the triceps brachii muscle was statistically significantly higher (p<0.05) during push-ups in position 1 and position 3 compared to position 5.
The mean activation value of the triceps brachii muscle reached its lowest value in position 5 compared to the other tested positions (p<0.05).

Push-ups performed in position 3 resulted in a smaller shift of the center of pressure (COP) along both the longitudinal X and lateral Y axes despite having a smaller support base than other positions.

core_principles.text: Maintain a straight trunk with active control and stabilization throughout the push-up to minimize unnecessary mechanical strain on the lumbar spine.

specific_findings.text: Maximum torque during push-up resistance represents more than 50% of the maximum force of the triceps brachii muscle, and can exceed 70% with adjustments in hand position.
Push-ups elicit significant activation of the serratus anterior muscle compared to other shoulder exercises.
Trapezius muscle activation during push-ups does not reach high essential muscular activity levels.
Activation levels of the biceps brachii and pectoralis major muscles do not significantly change with alterations in body position, extremity position, or support surface stability.
